Revert WIP-bundled Phase 4 commit f81f901; re-keep MeshV1 only

The previous commit f81f901 was intended to add only the MeshV1
Swift package (MeshTransport.swift, CodableRoundTripTests.swift,
INTEROP_TEST_MATRIX.md). However it accidentally bundled the
maintainer's in-flight WIP from `ios-native/` and `server/` that
was already staged in the local index. That WIP should not have
landed on `main` without a separate review pass.

This revert backs out everything from f81f901 except the three
MeshV1 files, which were the actual intended payload of that
commit. The maintainer's WIP for `ios-native/` and `server/` is
preserved locally in stash@{0} ("WIP before reverting Phase 4
bundle") and in the orphaned commit f81f901 in reflog; nothing
is lost.

End state:
  - main contains MeshV1/MeshTransport + Codable round-trip
    tests + INTEROP_TEST_MATRIX (the intended Phase 4 work).
  - main does NOT contain the ios-native / server WIP.
  - Local stash@{0} retains the WIP for the maintainer to
    review + commit separately.

Phase 4: iOS MeshTransport (v1 BLE) + Codable round-trip + interop matrix

- Sources/MeshV1/MeshTransport: v1-compliant CBPeripheralManager +
  CBCentralManager wrapper. Advertises the canonical service UUID
  (12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789ABC), serves the two characteristics
  per §A, scans for the same UUID, connects + subscribes to notify, and
  emits reassembled JSON via a Combine publisher. Mirrors the API of
  RAVEN-Android/modules/mesh/.../ble/BleMeshEngine.kt. Peer count exposed
  as a CurrentValueSubject so SwiftUI can bind.

  NOT a replacement for RAVEN/Services/MeshService.swift — that legacy
  service (using a different service UUID + simplified envelope) stays
  in place for now. Migration is the next Phase 4 step (Xcode-project
  side work, requires adding the MeshV1 package as a local dependency).

- Tests/MeshV1Tests/CodableRoundTripTests: 9 cases covering every §C
  envelope. Encode → decode → re-encode must be idempotent, and the
  encoded JSON must include every iOS-shipped short key (id, rm, sid,
  sn, rid, t, n, spk, ts, od, txt) for DM, and the long camelCase keys
  (originalMessageId, isACK, ...) for ACK. Catches CodingKeys typos
  before they cause silent wire breakage.

- INTEROP_TEST_MATRIX.md: 20-row test matrix for the test-lab person
  who'll run real-device cross-platform mesh testing. Unit-test row
  references (16+9+9 cases) and live-BLE row criteria (L1-L20). Plus
  setup notes, failure triage, and Phase 4 done criteria.

34/34 swift tests green.

MeshV1: add MeshSigner + verify-only signature tests

- Sources/MeshV1/MeshSigner: one-stop sign + verify wrapping CryptoKit's
  Curve25519.Signing over the 5 canonical signing rules. Mirrors
  RAVEN-Android/modules/mesh/.../signing/MeshSigner.kt API.
- Tests/MeshV1Tests/SharedVectorsSignatureTests: 9 new cases.

Important interop note encoded in the tests: Apple's Curve25519.Signing
uses RANDOMIZED Ed25519 (hedge nonces for side-channel + faulty-RNG
defense), so signing the same (key, message) twice yields two different
valid signatures. The deterministic shared-vectors signatures (from
Python's `cryptography` lib, matching BouncyCastle on Android) VERIFY
correctly under Apple's API — but Apple-produced signatures will not
byte-match the fixtures.

Tests therefore assert:
  1. Python-derived fixture signatures verify under Apple. ✓
  2. Apple-produced signatures round-trip via Apple's verifier. ✓
  3. Tampered inputs fail verification. ✓
Byte equality of Apple-signed sigs is intentionally not asserted.

25/25 swift tests pass.

RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1: Swift reference impl validated against shared-vectors/v1

What this is: a Swift Package implementing every wire-protocol layer in
`docs/MESH_PROTOCOL.md` v1 — envelopes, canonical signing (DM/Post/ACK/
Stop/Frame), chunking, dedup keys, spray-and-wait, pairing code,
fingerprint. Mirrors `RAVEN-Android/modules/mesh/`. Both implementations
now produce byte-identical output on the same shared-vectors fixtures.

What ships:
- RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1/Package.swift               (SPM library + test target)
- RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1/Sources/MeshV1/             (7 Swift files; iOS+Mac+Watch)
- RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1/Tests/MeshV1Tests/          (16 vector tests — 16/16 pass)
- RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1/Tests/MeshV1Tests/Resources/v1/
                                               (vendored snapshot of vectors)
- RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1/README.md
- tools/sync-vectors.sh                        (re-sync after vector regen)
- .gitignore                                   (whitelist MeshV1 under
                                                RAVEN-iOS/* exclude)

The legacy `RAVEN/Services/MeshService.swift` (different service UUID,
simplified envelope) is unchanged — it stays the live iOS impl until a
follow-up migrates it to consume MeshV1.

To run locally:
  swift test --package-path RAVEN-iOS/MeshV1

shared-vectors/v1: deterministic cross-platform RAVEN protocol fixtures

What this is: byte-exact JSON test vectors covering every wire-protocol
layer (crypto, canonicalization, envelopes, chunking, routing, trust)
derived from `docs/MESH_PROTOCOL.md` v1. Both iOS and Android consume
the same fixtures, so cross-platform interop becomes a unit-test problem
instead of a real-device debugging problem.

Layout:
  shared-vectors/
  ├── README.md, VERSIONING.md
  ├── generate_v1.py            (reproducible Python regenerator)
  └── v1/
      ├── identities.json       (Alice/Bob/Carol/Dave keys)
      ├── crypto/               (8 vectors)
      ├── canonicalization/     (6 vectors — 5 signing rules + DM-with-geo)
      ├── envelopes/            (6 vectors)
      ├── chunking/             (3 vectors)
      ├── routing/              (5 vectors)
      └── trust/                (2 vectors)

Determinism: RFC 8032 / 7748 test seeds, fixed timestamp 1700000000,
fixed nonces. Re-running generate_v1.py must produce byte-identical
files (verify with `git diff`).

iOS note: the current RAVEN-iOS MeshService.swift uses a different
service UUID and a simplified envelope (see RAVEN-iOS/RAVEN/Services/
MeshService.swift) — it does NOT implement MESH_PROTOCOL.md v1 today.
These vectors document the target spec; bringing iOS up to v1 is a
separate work item tracked under Android issue #1.

docs: bump README to v1.7, introduce ATSAM protocol, cross-link raven-security

v1.7 ships ATSAM, Raven's own layered security protocol for online and
offline messaging:

  1. Post-quantum hybrid pairing (X25519 + ML-KEM-768 / NIST FIPS 203)
  2. Private peer discovery (random-looking beacons to strangers)
  3. Live device confirmation (fresh-challenge replay defense)
  4. Encrypted mesh routing (rotating per-message recipient tags)
  5. Optional Vault Mode (one-time-pad content protection)

The full public-facing security documentation lives in the companion
repo at Raven-offline-messenger/raven-security:

  - Threat model
  - Per-layer security claims with limitations
  - Trust roadmap (6 stages)
  - Responsible disclosure policy
  - Test vector scaffolding
  - ATSAM Public Security Overview (PDF + Markdown)
Add CONTEXT.md — short summary for the cross-platform handoff

Add HANDOFF.md so the Windows cross-platform work can continue

Documents:
- What's done vs what's still missing (login, recipient picker, group UI,
  server endpoint deployment, custom tray icon)
- Likely first-build issues with concrete fixes
- 7 sequential milestones (M1 build → M7 installer + signing) with
  concrete time estimates and verification steps
- The exact iOS-side fix (BLEMeshEngine.swift:2447) needed for iOS to
  discover the Windows peer (LocalName vs ServiceData parsing gap)
- Cross-platform interop test rig + diagnostic order
- Hard rule: any wire-protocol change means coordinated v2 across all
  three implementations, never unilateral

Add RAVEN for Windows + cross-platform mesh interop

Windows port (lightweight client + full mesh node):
- .NET 8 + WinUI 3 with Mica/Acrylic backdrop and Liquid Glass aesthetic
- Three views: Feed (Echo Wall), Messages (DMs + groups), Account
- Tray-resident service so mesh stays alive when window closed

Mesh layer (full parity with iOS / Mac):
- BLE central + peripheral via WinRT GattServiceProvider
- Same wire protocol, GATT UUIDs, fragmentation, envelope format
- Direct mesh, multi-hop relay, and online bridge uplink for offline peers
- X25519 ECDH + HKDF-SHA-256 + AES-256-GCM + Ed25519 (BouncyCastle)
- SQLCipher local DB + DPAPI-protected key + token storage
- Group chat support: AES-256 group key + per-member envelope addressing
- Live mesh-stats counters (peers / frames-relayed / bridge-uplinks)

Cross-platform interop:
- New docs/MESH_PROTOCOL.md (590 lines) — single source of truth for the
  wire format, derived from the iOS Swift sources, with all known protocol
  quirks and v2 fix targets documented
- Mirror test suites (15 xUnit tests on Windows; matching XCTest stubs on
  iOS) verify byte-equal canonical signing data, AES-GCM combined layout,
  HKDF determinism, fingerprint format, and chunk-framer round-trip
- New server endpoint POST /api/mesh/bridge-envelope receives opaque
  envelopes from any platform's bridge and stores them for offline
  recipients (zero-knowledge — server never decrypts)
